# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete – Updated 91)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); **present day: military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing, with British army called up for campaign; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of that time of year**
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India, Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Bloomsbury, parsonage, forge, Brompton, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange, Coldcombe hill farms, Salford granary, Champ de Mars (France), barracks, Greek Street, Rectory

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher (Sharp); mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic and entertainer; kept father and associates laughing with fun and mimicry; used to fetch gin from public-house; known in studios in the quarter; described as "queer little wild vixen"
- **Secret Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license
- **Current Status**: Living with Rawdon in Brompton lodgings; marriage revealed through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs; denied access to Miss Crawley at Park Lane; letters sent back unopened
- **Mrs. Bute's Investigation**: Mrs. Bute tracked Rebecca back to Greek Street lodgings where father lived; gathered full account of Rebecca's parentage, education, and behaviour from landlady Mrs. Stokes; learned father was dissolute, poor, good-natured, amusing, hunted by bailiffs and duns; learned he did not marry Rebecca's mother until short time before her death
- **Mrs. Bute's Characterization of Rebecca**: Claims she is daughter of opera-girl and lost man; characterizes her as having been dancer and painter's model; brought up as befitted mother's daughter; claims knavery of pair is irremediable and properly conducted persons should never notice them

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate; selfish heavy dragoon
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license; living with her in Brompton lodgings furnished luxuriously
- **Current Status**: Awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; financial strain evident; denied door access by Mr. Bowls at Park Lane; won two hundred pounds from George Osborne at billiards at Cocoa-Tree
- **Character**: Shows contempt for Miss Crawley's aides-de-camp (Briggs, Firkin) with frankness; treats Firkin roughly (pulling off boots, sending her on errands in rain); makes coarse jokes; flings money as if an insult; contrasts sharply with Mrs. Bute's tactful treatment of same staff; **During his prosperity, obeyed only with sulky acquiescence; when disgrace came, nobody to help or pity him**

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces; liked Rawdon and Rebecca who amused her
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute Crawley's continuous nursing; not "coming-to"; never stirs out; unwell; door kept by Mr. Bowls; access denied to Rawdon and Rebecca; letters unopened
- **Mrs. Bute's Concern**: Mrs. Bute recognizes Miss Crawley is exceedingly unwell and cannot move for some weeks; fears old lady has secret longing to welcome back Rawdon and Rebecca; recognizes neither her own singing nor her girls' singing, nor her husband's manners, nor talk of dogs and horses can amuse Miss Crawley as Rebecca and Rawdon do; fears if taken to Rectory, Miss Crawley would grow angry and flee to Rawdon's clutches again
- **Overmanagement**: Mrs. Bute, through overeager management and severe authority for Miss Crawley's own good, has managed rather too well and made Miss Crawley more ill than necessary; harassed invalid succumbs to her authority but is inclined to escape at first chance; confinement to bed may add to her depression

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; declared Rebecca "artful little hussy"; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley; took vacant room at Park Lane; remains continuously present; guards access; wearing herself to death by foregoing sleep, dinner, fresh air
- **Strategy**: Consults Miss Briggs on matters of taste/difficulty; admires her poetry; shows appreciation through acts of kindness and politeness; transmutes small gifts into gold through compliments; encourages Briggs to expect "prodigious benefit" when she inherits, ensuring loyalty and support; expects to command loyalty and receive promotions from her promises, generosity, and kind words; garrison charmed to act under her leadership
- **Investigation of Rebecca**: Followed Rebecca back from Miss Pinkerton's to Greek Street lodgings; obtained full account from landlady Mrs. Stokes; spreading tale that Rebecca is daughter of opera-girl and dissolute painter; claims Rebecca has danced, been painter's model, drank gin, and moral is that knavery is irremediable
- **Thoughts and Plans**: Believes Rebecca too clever and spirited and desperate to submit without struggle; must prepare for combat and be incessantly watchful against assault, mine, or surprise; wishes her husband had head on shoulders to urge Miss Crawley to repent of free-thinking ways and cast off Rawdon; wishes him to induce Miss Crawley to benefit her own daughters and boys; fears Miss Crawley will escape to Rawdon's clutches at first chance

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Heartbreak and Current State**: Father ordered her to banish George and return all presents and letters; she promised but could not part with letters; brooded over them constantly, living in past life; letters are all she has left; looked to death with inexpressible longing
- **Engagement Rupture**: Broken off by John Osborne's veto; happiness and character compromised; society judges her as imprudent and criminal; faces reputation damage and isolation
- **Recent Events**: Has returned all presents George gave her through Dobbin—ring, silver knife (bought as boy at fair), gold chain, locket with hair; sent accompanying letter absolving George of blame and absolving him from engagement, noting father's orders and cruel suspicions of Mr. Osborne as hardest griefs to bear; lives at St. Adelaide Villas in reduced circumstances; appearance ghastly with pathetic look of despair; sits brooding silently over her letters; too sad to acknowledge attempts of Irish servant-maid to console her; trembling when seen by Dobbin

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant now ruined; proclaimed defaulter on Stock Exchange; declared bankrupt and commercially exterminated
- **Response to George-Amelia Affair**: When alluding to affair, spoke with bitterness nearly matching Mr. Osborne's; cursed Osborne family as heartless, wicked, ungrateful; swore no power on earth would induce him to marry his daughter to Osborne's son; ordered Emmy to banish George and return all presents and letters

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; proved most faithful consoler upon learning bankruptcy; has accepted reduced circumstances at St. Adelaide Villas; willing to receive Captain Dobbin; greatly agitated by arrival of piano, conjecturing it signal of amity from George; poured forth sorrows and complaints to Dobbin with great openness; cast back looks of anguish towards Dobbin when leading Amelia upstairs

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; adored by men; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement Status**: Broken off by his father's veto; received returned presents from Amelia (ring, silver knife, gold chain, locket with hair) with great despondency; fell into reviewing history of their lives together, seeing her from childhood as sweet, innocent, charmingly simple, artlessly fond and tender
- **Current Emotional State**: Experiencing sickening remorse and shame at his own selfishness and indifference contrasted with her perfect purity; spent hours with Dobbin discussing Amelia and their relationship; temporarily forgot about glory and war
- **Military Status**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase (vice Smith); now excited by Napoleon's escape and landing; bent upon doing duty and gaining share of honour and distinction; forms portion of British army being mobilized for campaign

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George Osborne's father; most determined and obstinate opponent at creditor meetings; harassed Sedley severely; put instant veto on George's intercourse with Amelia; menaced youth with maledictions if he broke commands; vilipended Amelia as "basest and most artful of vixens"
- **Motivation**: Must tell and believe lies against hated object to remain consistent with own actions; from sense of consistency, must prove fallen man wretched to justify own hard-heartedness, ingratitude, selfishness

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Carried off George Osborne from billiards; served as agent bidding for small square piano at Russell Square auction; successfully outbid Rawdon's agent; acquired piano for Amelia Sedley's benefit
- **Character and Feelings**: Infatuated with Amelia; blushed when jokingly asked if he would marry her; defended her passionately against ridicule; swore he would become uproused British lion if anyone spoke against her
- **Recent Actions**: Visited Mrs. Sedley at St. Adelaide Villas; listened with great sympathy to her complaints and misfortunes; condoled with her losses; agreed in reprehending Mr. Osborne's conduct; did not correct Mrs. Sedley's error in believing piano came from George; showed her the courage to ask to see Amelia; received returned presents from her; experienced inexpressible grief, pity, and terror upon seeing her ghastly appearance; described himself as criminal after visit; loves Amelia too fondly; soft-hearted, melted by sight of women and children in pain; broke into emotion upon seeing her condition
- **Military Status**: Forms portion of British army now being mobilized against Napoleon; quite as much excited as rest of regiment by Napoleon's escape; bent upon doing duty in his own quiet way

**Medical Professionals**
- **Mr. Clump** (apothecary): Attending Miss Crawley; conferred with Dr. Squills; advised Mrs. Bute that Miss Crawley not in state requiring bed confinement; depressed but not necessarily bedridden; recommended change, fresh air, gaiety as remedies; urged Mrs. Bute to persuade Miss Crawley to rise, take little drives; suggested such activity would restore roses to Mrs. Bute's own cheeks
- **Dr. Squills**: Consulting with Mr. Clump on Miss Crawley's condition

**Other Characters**
- **Miss Briggs**: Found marriage revelation letter on Rebecca's pincushion; read affecting document; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley; reported intelligence to Mrs. Bute; subject to Rawdon's contempt and coarse jokes; receives better treatment from Mrs. Bute who consults her on taste, admires her poetry, and promises future benefit
- **Firkin**: Miss Crawley's servant; treated roughly by Rawdon (pulling off boots, rain errands); receives small gifts from Mrs. Bute accompanied by compliments that transform them to gold in her heart; expects prodigious benefit from Mrs. Bute's future inheritance
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; widower who proposed to Rebecca; broke out in fury upon learning marriage; ransacked her room at Queen's Crawley
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; denies Rawdon and Rebecca access; returns letters unopened
- **Mr. Clapp**: Clerk of Mr. Sedley; found domicile with Sedley family at St. Adelaide Villas
- **Mrs. Blenkinsop**: Old servant; amassed considerable sum in service; staying with Sedley family without wages; tends them and grumbles
- **Edward Dale**: Young stockbroker; saw George at Opera; member of Messrs. Dale, Spiggot, and Dale of Threadneedle Street
- **Mrs. Stokes**: Landlady in Greek Street where Rebecca's father lived; communicative; told Mrs. Bute about Sharp's dissolute life, good nature, amusement value, persecution by bailiffs and duns, late marriage to Rebecca's mother, and Rebecca's wild vixen nature, mimicry, and familiarity with studios
- **Irish servant-maid**: Buxom girl at St. Adelaide Villas; made many trials to console Amelia; unsuccessful due to profound sadness
- **Mrs. Major O'Dowd**: Wife of Major in --th regiment; resolved to share campaign; hopes to write herself Mrs. Colonel O'Dowd, C.B. by campaign's end
- **Stubble and Spooney**: Officers in --th regiment; look to get their companies without purchase

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **ENGAGEMENT RUPTURE COMPLETE**: Amelia has returned all presents to George through Dobbin; sent letter absolving George of blame; engagement formally broken; George experiencing remorse and shame
- **DOBBIN'S DEVOTION**: Deeply infatuated with Amelia; soft-hearted; loves her too fondly; devastated by her condition
- **AMELIA'S DESPAIR**: Ghastly appearance with pathetic despair; brooding over letters; looking to death with longing; isolated and inconsolable
- **MILITARY MOBILIZATION**: Napoleon escaped and landed; British army called up; --th regiment mobilized; campaign imminent; George and Dobbin both bent on duty and honour
- **MISS CRAWLEY'S CONDITION**: Confined to bed; not recovering from marriage shock; completely cut off from Rawdon and Rebecca; under severe management by Mrs. Bute that may be counterproductive
- **MRS. BUTE'S STRATEGY AND CONCERNS**: Carefully cultivating staff loyalty through kindness and promises; making Miss Crawley more ill than necessary through overeager management; fears Rebecca and Rawdon will reclaim Miss Crawley at first opportunity; recognizes her own family cannot amuse Miss Crawley as Rebecca and Rawdon do; must maintain constant vigilance against Rebecca's expected assault
- **MEDICAL ADVICE**: Mr. Clump and Dr. Squills recommend Miss Crawley's confinement may add to depression; advise change, fresh air, gaiety, and little drives as remedies; suggest Mrs. Bute's own health suffering from overstrain
